t: For necessary expenses in carrying out uranium enrichment facility decontamination and decommissioning, remedial actions and other activities of title II of the Atomic Energy Act of 1954 and title X, subtitle A of the Energy Policy Act of 1992, $278,807,000, to be derived from the fund, to remain available until expended: Provided, That at least $42,000,000 of amounts derived from the fund for such expenses shall be expended in accordance with title X, subtitle A, of the Energy Policy Act of 1992.

fable.w: This is a pure appropriations provision that funds decontamination and decommissioning activities and directs how part of the money is spent. The tempting reading is that "remedial actions" or the reference to the Energy Policy Act implies involvement of outside parties, but the text itself sets out no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government.
fable.s: For necessary expenses in carrying out uranium enrichment facility decontamination and decommissioning, remedial actions and other activities

opus.w: This is a pure appropriation provision that funds decontamination, decommissioning, and remedial activities and earmarks at least $42,000,000 for title X, subtitle A. It sets up no process for anyone outside the federal government to consult on, comment on, or challenge a federal decision. The cross-reference to remedial actions that may pay outside licensees is at most a benefit or reimbursement program, which does not count as participation.
opus.s: $278,807,000, to be derived from the fund, to remain available until expended
opus.b: 1. **Analysis.** The tempting reading is that "remedial actions" under title X, subtitle A of the Energy Policy Act of 1992 involve outsiders, because that subtitle reimburses outside licensees for cleanup costs. That reading fails. This section only appropriates money and earmarks part of it. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue. Even if the cross-referenced program pays outside parties, applying for reimbursement is an application for benefits, and the definition excludes that.

qwen_chat.w: This section is an appropriations provision that authorizes the expenditure of funds for specific activities (decontamination, decommissioning, remedial actions). It does not contain any language requiring or recommending consultation, coordination, or participation with entities outside the federal government (such as states, tribes, the public, or independent experts). The reference to 'title II of the Atomic Energy Act' and 'title X... of the Energy Policy Act' points to other statutory authorities but does not itself establish a participation mechanism in this text. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "carrying out... remedial actions" implies coordination with outside parties (e.g., contractors or local communities). However, the text itself only authorizes the expenditure of funds and references other statutes for the scope of work. It does not explicitly mandate consultation, public comment, or advisory boards involving non-federal entities in this specific section. The actors mentioned are the fund and the statutes themselves. There is no mention of states, tribes, the public, or independent experts participating in the decision-making process within this text.
